outline: 114 Continuous Random Variables and Relative Frequency
1893 Median and Quartiles using the CDF

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has CDF $F(x)=\frac{x^{3}-8}{208}$ on $[2,6]$. Find the median, both quartiles and the 40th percentile, correct to two decimal places.
A continuous random variable has CDF $F(x)=\frac{x^{2}-4x}{32}$ on $[4,8]$. Find its exact median and a two decimal place approximation.
A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\frac{x-2}{18}$ on $[2,8]$, and zero elsewhere. Find its CDF on $[2,8]$, then find the exact median and first quartile.
examples.solution_text:
Integrate from the lower boundary of the support.
$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\int_2^x\frac{t-2}{18}\,dt\\&=\left[\frac{(t-2)^2}{36}\right]_2^x\\&=\frac{(x-2)^2}{36},\qquad2\le x\le8\end{aligned}$
For the median, set $F(m)=\frac12$.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{(m-2)^2}{36}&=\frac12\\(m-2)^2&=18\\m&=2\pm3\sqrt2\end{aligned}$
Since $m\in[2,8]$, the median is $m=2+3\sqrt2$.
For the first quartile, set $F(Q_1)=\frac14$.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{(Q_1-2)^2}{36}&=\frac14\\(Q_1-2)^2&=9\\Q_1&=2\pm3\end{aligned}$
Reject $Q_1=-1$, which is outside the support. Hence $Q_1=5$.

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\frac{2(4-x)}{16}$ on $[0,4]$, and zero elsewhere. Find the exact median and explain why it is not $2$.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{2(4-t)}{16}\,dt\\&=\frac18\left[4t-\frac{t^2}{2}\right]_0^x\\&=\frac{8x-x^2}{16},\qquad0\le x\le4\end{aligned}$
Set $F(m)=\frac12$.
$\begin{aligned}\frac{8m-m^2}{16}&=\frac12\\m^2-8m+8&=0\\m&=\frac{8\pm\sqrt{64-32}}2\\m&=4\pm2\sqrt2\end{aligned}$
Reject $4+2\sqrt2$, which is outside $[0,4]$. The median is $m=4-2\sqrt2$.
$F(2)=\frac{16-4}{16}=\frac34$, so $2$ has three quarters of the probability below it. Half the probability is reached before the midpoint.

examples.question_text: The time $X$ minutes for a process to finish has PDF $f(x)=\frac{3(6-x)^2}{216}$ on $[0,6]$, and zero elsewhere. Find the median time, correct to two decimal places, and interpret it.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}F(x)&=\int_0^x\frac{3(6-t)^2}{216}\,dt\\&=\left[-\frac{(6-t)^3}{216}\right]_0^x\\&=1-\frac{(6-x)^3}{216},\qquad0\le x\le6\end{aligned}$
Set $F(m)=\frac12$.
$\begin{aligned}1-\frac{(6-m)^3}{216}&=\frac12\\(6-m)^3&=108\\6-m&=\sqrt[3]{108}\\m&=6-\sqrt[3]{108}\\m&\approx1.24\end{aligned}$
The median lies in $[0,6]$. Half of the processes finish within approximately $1.24$ minutes.

examples.derivation: Solving F(x)=p gives x³=8+208p. Thus m=∛112≈4.82, Q1=∛60≈3.91, Q3=∛164≈5.47 and the 40th percentile is ∛91.2≈4.50. All lie in [2,6]; plotted quartile coordinates agree.
F(m)=1/2 gives m²−4m−16=0, with roots 2±2√5. Only 2+2√5 lies in [4,8], giving m≈6.47.
Integrating from 2 gives F(x)=(x−2)²/36. The median roots are 2±3√2, so m=2+3√2. First-quartile roots are 2±3; rejecting −1 gives Q1=5.
Integration gives F(x)=(8x−x²)/16. F(m)=1/2 gives m²−8m+8=0, hence m=4−2√2 after rejecting the other root. F(2)=3/4 confirms that 2 is not the median.
Integration gives F(x)=1−(6−x)³/216. Setting F(m)=1/2 gives m=6−∛108≈1.24 minutes. This lies in [0,6] and correctly identifies the time within which half the processes finish.
The first interval contributes 3/12=1/4. In the second interval F(x)=1/4+(x−3)/4. Solving F(m)=1/2 gives m=4. The plotted CDF passes through (3,1/4), (4,1/2) and (6,1).
For total frequency 80, quartile levels are 20 and 60. Linear interpolation gives Q1=10+(12/24)×10=15 cm and Q3=30+(4/16)×10=32.5 cm. IQR=17.50 cm; both diagram guides intersect the correct segments.
